items.title: Ernest Roubleau Interview, 1961-10-18
items.q: My father helped me with the violin because he told me one day, he says, why don't you try to learn how to play some music?

ctx.x: What violin? I play violin too. Yes. Yes. Did you have lessons? Your father helped you with that? Or how did you learn that?

My father helped me with the violin because he told me one day, he says, why don't you try to learn how to play some music? So I said to him, I says, I don't believe I'm going to learn that. So he said, yeah, try. I believe you can learn it. Well, I used to watch him playing his violin. After he'd go to work, and I know where he saved the violin right on top of the almo. You know, it was all the time. He put it up there, and I told my mother. I told my mother, I said, I said, Mama, I said, get the violin down and…
Yeah, I didn't know you ever played that one.
